title: Where the model's error backlog actually sits
headline_insight: The single largest slice of the model's cumulative error is early-inning coin-flip games -- MLB innings 1-3 at a .4-.6 model probability carries 6063.25 in total absolute residual mass (mean_abs_residual 0.4912 over 12,344 rows).
what_it_means: Ranking every sport x game-state x probability-band segment by total absolute error shows the improvement backlog is concentrated where little has happened and the outcome is genuinely uncertain -- early, near-50/50 states. That is where fixing the model would remove the most cumulative error.
how_to_read: Each segment reports n rows, mean absolute residual, and total_abs_residual_mass (n times mean); the ranked list puts the biggest total error slices first.
why_it_matters: It turns a vague 'the model is off' into a prioritized to-do list -- the top segments are all early-to-mid MLB innings in the uncertain probability bands.
caveat: No significance test here; total residual mass scales with row count, so high-volume buckets rank high partly by size, not only by per-row error. edge_claimed false.
